minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  November 8, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:02 p.m., on November 8, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on November 3, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:50 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:04 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:01 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

City Council Minutes  1  November 8, 2016
 PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sharon Genton, City Liaison for Rock Harbor Church, M.V.: discussed various services that Rock
Harbor Church offers, including a prayer walk, school makeovers, Saturday tutoring, participating
in the meals on wheels program and volunteering at city events. She invited residents to come out
and help the church fight the battle against litter and debris on November 12, 2016, beginning
at 9:00 a.m. at Sycamore Park.

Philip Bettencourt, Saunders Property Company, Newport Beach: stated that he is a contract
planning professional for the Saunders Property Company and they are carefully evaluating
properties in Mission Viejo. His company is following lessons learned from the Kosmont study
and looking at the City's vision plan process and he stated that there are great days ahead for the
City of Mission Viejo.

Ginny Aitkens, M.V.: announced that the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library will host its annual
holiday book sale on November 21, 2016, from 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2 and 5 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated October 21, 2016 in the Amount of $1,890,499.88

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Biennial City Commission Member Term Expiration

  (1) Directed the City Clerk to post the Notice of City Commission Vacancies, (2) set
  application deadline for January 4, 2017, and (3) scheduled appointment of commission
  members for January 10, 2017.
City Council Minutes  2  November 8, 2016
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht stated that she is concerned about the flavor of the wording under
  the Staff Reports section on page 7 of the Minutes. She said that the verbiage used is an
  unfavorable reflection of her and it should be noted that the City lost two hearings so the
  illegal parking of her RV was not illegal.

  Mayor Ury said that she is expressing her view that it was a legal loss versus a continuation
  for some clerical clean-up. He suggested that Council Member Schlicht submit, to the City
  Clerk, whatever documentation she would like to add to the public record.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the Minutes
  for the regular City Council meeting of October 25, 2016, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, and Ury
  NOES:  Schlicht
  ABSENT:  None

5.  Revisions to City of Mission Viejo Personnel Policies

  Council Member Schlicht asked if any of the revisions are due to non-compliance with
  Federal or State law.

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas responded that staff is adding language
  to clarify actual practices but all policies are in compliance with Federal and State laws.
  She noted that the Deferred Compensation Policy is a new policy.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Mayor Ury, to adopt Resolution
  16-51 Providing for the Revisions to select Personnel Policies.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

6.  Proposed Regular and Urgency Ordinances Adopting the 2016 California Building
  Codes, the International Swimming Pool And Spa Code and the International
  Property Maintenance Code
City Council Minutes  3  November 8, 2016
   City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report and Building Official Jay Elbettar
  answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Motion made by Mayor Ury, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to (1) adopt Urgency
  Ordinance 16-317 Adopting by reference the 2016 Editions of the California Building,
  Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards, Historical
  Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2015 Editions of the International
  Swimming Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, together,
  with certain Appendices and Amendments thereto, and amending Title 8 of the Mission
  Viejo Municipal Code; (2) adopt Urgency Ordinance 16-318 Adopting by Reference the
  2016 California Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions; (3)
  introduce Ordinance 16-319 Adopting by reference the 2016 Editions of the California
  Building, Residential, Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards,
  Historical Building, and Existing Building Codes, and the 2015 Editions of the
  International Swimming Pool and Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code,
  together, with certain Appendices and Amendments thereto, and amending Title 8 of the
  Mission Viejo Municipal Code; (4) introduce Ordinance 16-320 Adopting by Reference
  the 2016 California Fire Code, Together with Certain Amendments and Deletions; and (5)
  schedule a Public Hearing for December 13, 2016 to Adopt the Ordinances Identified
  above.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

7.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs shared video of an arson fire which depicts the driver of a pickup
  truck throwing a firework and igniting a tree and vegetation next to a home in Mission
  Viejo. He said OCFA is still looking for the suspect and asked for the public's assistance
  if they can identify the vehicle. .

  Battalion Chief John Abel, OCFA: discussed the open arson case that was shown in the
  video, the wild land fire situation in the State, fire season, and the OCFA Urban Search and
  Rescue Program.

8.  Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)

  Mayor Ury stated that he serves on the Regional Planning and Highways Committee which
  recently recommended awarding a $1.2 billion design-build contract to OC 405
City Council Minutes  4  November 8, 2016
   Partners. Mayor Ury said the entire OCTA Board will vote on the contract next week and
  he will have a more complete report at the next City Council meeting.

9.  Update On CUSD Bond Measure Issue

  There was no report.

STAFF REPORTS

There were no staff reports.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths had no comments.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that the third community workshop for the City's Vision Plan
will take place on Thursday, November 10, 2016, at 6:30 p.m. in the Saddleback Room at city
hall. The workshop will focus on a series of strategies for envisioning the core area as well as
three vision concept alternatives that show how the strategies may be realized. Council Member
Sachs said the Economic Development Committee received a short presentation on the process and
it is very interesting. He also encouraged community members to attend and let their voices be
heard.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht read a prepared statement regarding the City's lawsuit against her for
the parking of her RV. She said that the Council has conspired with the City Attorney to badger
and harass her mom and her sister over an RV that is not even in the City. She said the real purpose
of the lawsuit is to defeat her in the election. Council Member Schlicht stated that the City has lost
three times in court and failed to carry its burden of establishing a probability of succeeding on the
merits of its claims at trial, as required. She concluded with a quote from Romans 13:1, "Let
everyone be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except that which God
has established. The authorities that exist have been established by God."

City Council Minutes  5  November 8, 2016
 Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum asked when the City can host another Neighborhood Watch Town Hall
meeting. She said she has received some inquires about issues around town and she'd like to look
at a date in the next few months. With the holidays approaching and packages being delivered to
homes, she feels that the City should provide a message at the next City Council Meeting on best
practices. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum also asked when the initial meeting on the Aquatics Center
will be held so that the budget oversight committee, consisting of herself and Council Member
Sachs, can participate. Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay said that
the meeting will be held sometime in December and he will be in touch with potential dates. Mayor
Pro Tem Bucknum invited residents to the City’s Veterans Day ceremony which will be held on
Friday, November 11, at 2:00 p.m. and in closing, she said that she hopes that when the election is
over, those that are elected and those that are not elected will continue to serve the City with a
servant’s heart.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury discussed the 2016 wheelchair tennis tournament which was held at the Marguerite
Tennis Center. He shared the trophy that the International Tennis Federation presented to the City
in recognition of the four years that Mission Viejo has hosted the event. Mayor Ury noted that
there were 36 world-class athletes representing twelve countries and he thanked staff for all of the
hard work.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 6:43 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, November 22, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of November 22, 2016

City Council Minutes  6  November 8, 2016
